context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Stop calling JSON.parse on req.params.id. It accepts arrays and objects, so a request like /api/Recycles/[1,2,3] or an operator object can return other users' recycle records (which include addresses and other Personal Data). Put authentication middleware (for example security.isAuthorized()) on every method of the /api/Recycles routes. Read the identifier as a plain integer and reject anything else: const id = Number.parseInt(req.params.id, 10); if (!Number.isInteger(id) || String(id) !== req.params.id) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Invalid id' }). Take ownership from the verified session or token and never from the path or body: const user = security.authenticatedUsers.from(req); if (!user) return res.status(401).end(). Then scope the query to that user: RecycleModel.findOne({ where: { id, UserId: user.data.id } }).then((recycle) => { if (!recycle) return res.status(404).end(); res.json({ status: 'success', data: recycle }) }). Only allow a wider lookup when the user holds an authorised role (for example user.data.role === 'admin'), and check that role on the server. Apply the same ownership check to the list, create, update and delete handlers on this route. For create, set UserId from the session and ignore any UserId sent in req.body. Add tests that check a request without authentication returns 401, a request for another user's id returns 404, and an array or object in the id parameter returns 400.
